sections.title: Startups and Their Contribution to the Nation

slides.title: What Is a Business Plan
slides.kicker: Every great business starts with an idea to innovate
bullets: A business plan is a written document, a blueprint explaining the goals of the business and the steps to achieve them.
It guides the entrepreneur from the initial idea stage to successfully starting and running the business.
It is a roadmap for decision making: stay organised, set priorities, and work systematically to grow.

slides.title: Eight Key Questions
slides.kicker: The bakery plan starts with eight careful questions
bullets: Needs and idea: what do people need, can it be produced, and what problem does it solve?
Also think about customers, money and costs, location, human resources, pricing, promotion, and risks.
Funding can come from friends, family, or investors, and selling can happen at a store or online.
slides.note: Eight questions before the first cupcake is baked.

slides.title: Know Your Bakery Customers
slides.kicker: Right product for the right people wins
bullets: Do customers prefer fresh bread, cakes, pastries, or healthier options like whole wheat products?
Specialise: cupcakes for children, savoury snacks for young adults, or everyday breads for families.
Fresh, affordable, or unique baked goods can offer what was not available in the area before.

slides.title: Money, Risks and Planning
slides.kicker: A robust financial start needs planning
bullets: Money and costs: how much money is needed, what are the costs, and who will fund it?
Pricing and profits: decide the price and work out how much profit can be made.
Challenges and risks: identify threats to operations and causes of loss before they strike.
slides.note: Risk soch lo abhi, loss baad mein nahi jheena.

slides.title: Four Pillars of Business
slides.kicker: Every successful business runs on four key pillars
bullets: The main functional areas are management and operations, finance and accounting, human resources, and marketing and sales.
Each area has a specific function and helps the business run smoothly.
Together, the four pillars turn goals into growth.

slides.title: Meet the Four Areas
slides.kicker: Each pillar has its own speciality
bullets: Human resources manages people; marketing and sales spreads awareness and drives sales.
Management and operations run the daily work; finance and accounting guard the money.
Knowing each area helps you decide who does what in your bakery.
slides.note: Har pillar ki apni duty hai.

slides.title: Why Areas Matter
slides.kicker: Structure and coordination help a business grow
bullets: Functional areas improve decision making and ensure resources are used properly.
They provide structure and better coordination across the whole business.
When each area does its job well, the business grows successfully.

slides.title: Human Resources at Work
slides.kicker: Right people, right skills, right attitude
bullets: Human resources manages people; the key focus is the right people and skills.
Examples: hiring new staff, managing employee benefits, and handling workplace conflict resolution.
Good HR keeps the team happy so the bakery runs without trouble.

slides.title: Management and Operations
slides.kicker: Plan well, deliver fresh, waste nothing
bullets: Management plans, organises, and guides the use of resources to achieve goals like market share through customer satisfaction.
Operations focuses on producing and delivering goods or services efficiently and on time.
Bakery work: choose the right equipment, arrange ingredients, monitor quality, and plan daily production.
slides.note: Fresh bakes, no delay, no wastage.

slides.title: Finance Pays the Bills
slides.kicker: Money planning keeps the ovens running
bullets: Finance is the management of money: planning, obtaining, and using funds to operate and grow.
Fixed costs stay constant: rent and equipment like ovens, mixers, and refrigerators.
Variable costs change with output: ingredients and packaging. Also plan investment and cash flow.
slides.note: Rent to dena hi hai, chahe ek cake bike.

slides.title: Accounting Tells the Truth
bullets: Accounting records, organises, and reports the business financial transactions.
Track money coming in (revenue) and money going out (expenses), and keep records correct.
The profit and loss account, or income statement, shows whether the business made a profit or a loss.
Investment means putting money into a venture expecting future income, profit, or value appreciation.

slides.title: Marketing and Sales
slides.kicker: Attract customers, then convince them to buy
bullets: The marketing and sales team helps attract customers and convinces them to buy the products.
Bakery moves: choose a catchy name, promote the business on social media, and offer discounts.

slides.title: Simple Winning Strategies
bullets: Create unique or seasonal items and customised desserts like a mango-flavoured cake.
Use social media to share photos and videos for awareness; offer discounts, deals, or special offers.
Provide easy online ordering and delivery; promote eco-friendly practices like recyclable packaging.

slides.title: India's Trading Communities
slides.kicker: Entrepreneurship runs deep in our roots
bullets: Skills, occupations, and occupational knowledge have been passed down through generations.
Long before modern startups, traditional communities practised self-employment, innovation, and trade.
These communities formed the backbone of India's local economy.
slides.note: Startup se pehle, seva aur vyapar.

slides.title: The Chettiar Story
bullets: The Nattukottai Chettiar community of Tamil Nadu were traders, bankers, and moneylenders.
They operated across India, Sri Lanka, Burma (now Myanmar), Malaysia, and Southeast Asia.
Known for trust-based lending, excellent record-keeping, and reinvesting profits into trade, temples, education, and welfare.
They built wealth through trade in salt, rice, textiles, and finance, often without formal banks.

slides.title: Failure Is a Teacher
bullets: Some startups grow rapidly while others struggle or even close down.
There is nothing wrong with failure if an honest effort has been made; every attempt teaches lessons.
Swami Vivekananda said: Arise, awake and stop not till the goal is reached.
slides.note: Girna buri baat nahi, rukna buri baat hai!

slides.title: India's Startup Power
slides.kicker: Third-largest startup ecosystem in the world
bullets: Powered by its young and talented population, India is the third-largest startup ecosystem in the world.
Around 120 unicorns (startups valued at over 1 billion dollars) in 2025 work in e-commerce, fin-tech, health-tech, and agri-tech.
Major hubs: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR.

slides.title: Government Schemes
slides.kicker: Startup India backs a self-reliant India
bullets: Startup India supports the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat: self-reliance through innovation and local solutions.
Atmanirbhar Bharat, launched in 2020, aims to make the country self-sustaining, boost domestic manufacturing, and reduce import dependency.
Viksit Bharat 2047 envisions a fully developed India by 2047, marking 100 years of independence.

slides.title: Startups Serve the Nation
slides.kicker: Jobs, taxes, and a better life
bullets: Startups create jobs and income for households and pay taxes to the government.
They improve quality of life through medicines, transportation, technology, and innovations.
They support sustainability and drive economic growth towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
slides.note: Agle founder shayad aap hi ho!

flashcards.front: What is entrepreneurship?
flashcards.back: A process through which individuals, or a group of individuals, convert a potential idea into a business venture.

flashcards.front: What is a business plan?
flashcards.back: A written document, a blueprint explaining the goals of the business and the steps to achieve them.

flashcards.front: Name four considerations while making a business plan.
flashcards.back: Needs and idea, potential customers, money and costs, location, human resources, pricing, promotion, and risks.

flashcards.front: Who can fund a new business, per the book?
flashcards.back: Funding sources can include friends, family, and investors.

flashcards.front: Give a bakery example of understanding customer needs.
flashcards.back: Check whether customers prefer fresh bread, cakes, pastries, or healthier options like whole wheat products.

flashcards.front: What are the four functional areas of a business?
flashcards.back: Management and operations, finance and accounting, human resources, and marketing and sales.

flashcards.front: How do functional areas help a business?
flashcards.back: They improve decision making, ensure resources are used properly, and give structure and coordination for growth.

flashcards.front: Complete the line: every successful business runs on four key pillars. Together, they turn what into what?
flashcards.back: They turn goals into growth.

flashcards.front: What is the key focus of human resources?
flashcards.back: The right people and skills: hiring staff, managing employee benefits, and handling workplace conflict resolution.

flashcards.front: Define fixed cost.
flashcards.back: Expenses that remain constant regardless of production or sales levels, like rent, salaries, or insurance.

flashcards.front: Define variable cost.
flashcards.back: Expenses that change in direct proportion to the volume of goods produced or sold, like raw materials and packaging.

flashcards.front: What does operations handle in a bakery?
flashcards.back: Choosing equipment, arranging ingredients, monitoring quality, and planning daily production without delay or wastage.

flashcards.front: What is the profit and loss account?
flashcards.back: An important accounting record, also called the income statement, showing whether the business made a profit or a loss.

flashcards.front: Define investment.
flashcards.back: Allocating money or resources into an asset, venture, or project expecting future income, profit, or value appreciation.

flashcards.front: What is the job of the marketing and sales team?
flashcards.back: To attract customers and convince them to buy, using a catchy name, social media, and discounts.

flashcards.front: Name three marketing strategies from the book.
flashcards.back: Seasonal desserts like mango-flavoured cake, social media photos and videos, and easy online ordering with delivery.

flashcards.front: Which Tamil Nadu community is famous for trade and banking?
flashcards.back: The Chettiar (Nattukottai Chettiar) community, known as traders, bankers, and moneylenders.

flashcards.front: What were the Chettiars known for?
flashcards.back: Trust-based lending, excellent accounting and record-keeping, and reinvesting profits into trade, temples, education, and welfare.

flashcards.front: What is a unicorn?
flashcards.back: A startup valued at over 1 billion dollars; India had around 120 unicorns in 2025.

flashcards.front: What is Atmanirbhar Bharat?
flashcards.back: A national policy framework launched in 2020 to make India self-sustaining, boost domestic manufacturing, and reduce import dependency.

flashcards.front: What is Viksit Bharat 2047?
flashcards.back: The government's vision to transform India into a fully developed nation by 2047, marking 100 years of independence.

flashcards.front: How should entrepreneurs treat failure?
flashcards.back: There is nothing wrong with failure if the effort is honest; each unsuccessful attempt teaches lessons for better businesses.

quiz.q: A business plan is best described as a:
options: Written document explaining business goals and the steps to achieve them
Secret recipe list of the bakery
Government tax form filed every year
quiz.why: The book calls it a written document, a blueprint of goals and the steps to achieve them.

quiz.q: Which question belongs under the 'Needs and Idea' part of a plan?
options: What problem does our product solve?
How much rent will the shop pay?
Which TV channel will show our advertisement?
How many workers should we hire?
quiz.why: Needs and Idea asks what people need, whether it can be produced, and what problem it solves.

quiz.q: While identifying potential customers for a bakery, whom might you target?
quiz.why: The book suggests cupcakes for children, savoury snacks for young adults, and breads for families.

quiz.q: Why does an entrepreneur keep using the business plan even after opening?
options: As a roadmap for decisions, priorities, and systematic growth
To guarantee that no competitor will ever open nearby
To fix the market price of lemons
To avoid keeping any financial records
quiz.why: The plan serves as a guide and roadmap for decision making, helping the business grow.

quiz.q: Which set correctly lists the four functional areas of a business?
options: Management and operations, finance and accounting, human resources, marketing and sales
quiz.why: The book groups business questions into these four main functional areas.

quiz.q: Functional areas mainly help a business by:
options: Improving decision making and using resources properly
Removing the need for a business plan
quiz.why: Each area has a specific function and improves decision making and resource use.

quiz.q: According to the book, the four pillars together:
options: Turn goals into growth with structure and coordination
Work separately and never share information
quiz.why: Together they provide structure, better coordination, and help the business grow successfully.

quiz.q: The key focus of the human resources area is:
options: Getting the right people and skills
quiz.why: Human resources manages people, with the key focus on right people and skills.

quiz.q: Which of these is a fixed cost for the bakery?
quiz.why: Fixed costs stay constant regardless of output; the book lists rent as an example.

quiz.q: Variable costs are best defined as expenses that:
options: Change in direct proportion to the volume produced or sold
Never change no matter what happens
Are kept aside only for paying taxes
quiz.why: Variable costs rise as production rises and fall as production falls, like raw materials.

quiz.q: In accounting, the money coming into a business is called:
quiz.why: Accounting tracks money coming in (revenue) and money going out (expenses).

quiz.q: Which of the following correctly describes investment?
options: Putting money into a venture expecting future income or value growth
Paying the monthly rent on time
Keeping all cash locked in a drawer
Spending the entire profit on a party
quiz.why: Investment allocates money into an asset or project expecting future income, profit, or appreciation.

quiz.q: The main job of the marketing and sales team is to:
options: Attract customers and convince them to buy
Bake the bread fresh each morning
quiz.why: Marketing and sales attracts customers and convinces them to buy the products.

quiz.q: Which dessert does the book give as an example of a customised, seasonal item?
quiz.why: The book suggests creating unique or seasonal items like a mango-flavoured cake.

quiz.q: Historically, the Chettiar community worked as:
quiz.why: Chettiars were traders, bankers, and moneylenders across India and Southeast Asia.

quiz.q: Why do the Chettiars still inspire modern India?
options: Risk-taking, discipline, and long-term vision built sustainable businesses
They never faced any business risk
quiz.why: The book says Chettiar entrepreneurship shows how risk-taking, discipline, and vision build sustainable businesses.

quiz.q: Atmanirbhar Bharat was launched by the government in:
quiz.why: Atmanirbhar Bharat is a national policy framework launched in 2020.

quiz.q: A unicorn is:
options: A startup valued at over 1 billion dollars
A startup valued at over 1 crore rupees
A company more than 100 years old
A startup that has no employees
quiz.why: The book defines unicorns as startups valued at over 1 billion dollars.

quiz.q: Which cities does the book name as major startup hubs?
quiz.why: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR have become major startup hubs.

quiz.q: The Startup India scheme supports the vision of:
quiz.why: Startup India supports Atmanirbhar Bharat, making India self-reliant through innovation.

quiz.q: According to the book, startup ventures are creating:
quiz.why: These ventures create jobs, support sustainability, and drive economic growth.

examples.title: Nimbu Pani Stall Profit Report
examples.problem: For the school festival's Young Entrepreneurs Challenge, you and your classmates run a nimbu pani stall. You spend Rs 300 on lemons and sugar and Rs 100 on glasses for the day. You sell 120 glasses at Rs 5 each. Prepare the expense and profit report for your class teacher.
steps: List the costs: lemons and sugar Rs 300 (they change with how much you make, a variable cost) and glasses Rs 100 (fixed for the day).
Compute revenue: 120 glasses x Rs 5 = Rs 600 (money coming in).
Profit is money earned after paying costs: 600 - 400 = Rs 200.
Also note feedback: most visitors liked the drink, so the idea works.
examples.answer: The stall made a profit of Rs 200, reported to the class teacher with the expense list.

examples.title: Business Plan for the Bakery
examples.problem: You and your friends want to open a bakery offering snacks and desserts. Use the eight key considerations from the chapter to prepare the business plan.
steps: Needs and idea: people want fresh, affordable baked goods not available in the area; it solves the problem of no fresh bakery nearby.
Potential customers: cupcakes for children, savoury snacks for young adults, everyday breads for families.
Money and costs: funding from friends, family, and investors; plan fixed costs like rent and ovens, variable costs like ingredients and packaging.
Location: decide where it will be made and whether to sell at a store or online.
Human resources: list how many people are needed and the skills required, like a baker.
Pricing and profits: set the price so that profit can be made after paying costs.
Promotion: advertise through social media with photos and videos, and offer discounts.
Challenges and risks: note threats to operations, like rising ingredient costs, and plan for them.
examples.answer: A complete business plan: a written blueprint of goals and steps that guides the bakery from idea to running business.

examples.title: Sort Tasks into Functional Areas
examples.problem: A bakery owner does these four tasks this week. Identify which functional area each task belongs to: (a) hiring a new assistant baker, (b) recording revenue and expenses in the profit and loss account, (c) planning daily production and checking ingredient quality, (d) promoting a mango-flavoured cake on social media.
steps: Task (a) is about people and skills, so it belongs to Human Resources.
Task (b) is recording, organising, and reporting financial transactions, so it belongs to Finance and Accounting.
Task (c) is producing and delivering efficiently and on time, so it belongs to Management and Operations.
Task (d) is spreading awareness to attract customers, so it belongs to Marketing and Sales.
examples.answer: (a) Human Resources, (b) Finance and Accounting, (c) Management and Operations, (d) Marketing and Sales.
